title: Symbolic matrix differentiation loses terms and mishandles matrix components
provenance: Public historical case. Evaluator-authored problem-only adaptation and synthesis of original SymPy issue reports #24021, #25118, #24725, #23492, #23931, #23364 and related matrix-derivative reports referenced by upstream PR #25150, retrieved 2026-10-05. Current issue bodies are not authenticated pre-fix snapshots. Solution descriptions, implementation names and comments are omitted.
body: Several public matrix-differentiation operations return zero, lose terms, raise exceptions or have the wrong shape despite ordinary component calculus giving a well-defined answer. For a square MatrixSymbol E, diff(trace(E)**2 + trace(E*E.T), E) returns zero even though differentiating the addends separately works; the sum should give 2*trace(E)*Identity(E.rows) + 2*E. Adding scalar constants or affine terms must not erase derivatives. For an n-by-1 MatrixSymbol v, a nonsymmetric explicit coefficient matrix B and explicit column c, the gradient of v.T*B*v + v.T*c + k*Identity(1) must equal (B+B.T)*v + c and its Hessian must agree with explicit component calculus. Apply scalar chain rules to reciprocals and negative integer powers of a trace; preserve the derivative shape. The Jacobian of v/trace(v.T*v) must agree with differentiating its entries. Matrix elements must behave as independent coordinates: differentiating a matrix with respect to its own (i,j) entry, or differentiating that entry with respect to the matrix, gives the correctly shaped single-entry basis matrix; unrelated matrix symbols give zero. This also applies to rectangular matrices, sums and scalar multiples. Differentiating a positive integer power of an explicit matrix that depends on a scalar must preserve factor order, including noncommuting bases; exponent zero gives a zero matrix. Mixed expressions involving a MatrixSymbol and its explicit entries must yield tensor derivatives with correct axes and entries. Repair these related public behaviors and add regression tests. Preserve ordinary scalar differentiation, supported existing matrix derivatives, and zero derivatives for independent variables.
